"What is the action being performed?
One person among the monks answered according to the matter:
"The *karmavācanā* (formal ritual act) for so-and-so."
This is because there is no method for establishing a boundary without the formal act of receiving consent (*chanda*).
Furthermore, regarding the establishment of a boundary, two realms cannot be joined directly; one must leave a space between them.
Nor may a boundary be established across a swift-flowing river, except where a permanent bridge exists.

If a *sīmāmaṇḍala* (ordination platform) is established within a *mahāsīmā* (great boundary), first erect the four boundary markers for the *sīmāmaṇḍala*. Then, outside of these, at a distance of one cubit (*hasta*) from the base, erect the internal boundary markers of the *mahāsīmā*; further outward, according to the proximity or distance, also erect the four boundary markers.
An elder monk who has long resided there should announce the boundaries; from among the assembly, one capable of performing the *karmavācanā* (formal ritual) should be appointed to establish them.
One should first establish the great boundary (*mahāsīmā*) and subsequently establish the *śīmaṇḍala* (ordination site).

If one wishes to proclaim the characteristics of this great boundary (mahā-sīmā), one should first proceed clockwise around the four directions starting from the southeast corner of the outer boundary;
then, one should likewise proclaim the inner boundary, also completing one circuit.
He says:
"That is the external boundary marker; this is the internal boundary marker. This completes one circuit of the inner and outer markers of the great boundary.
Thus he proclaims three times.
If there is no inner boundary (sīmā) within, one should simply announce the outer marks.

Regarding the method for establishing the large and small boundaries, the Saṃgha must assemble in its entirety; the acceptance of proxy votes (chanda) is not permitted. This is because those who accept proxy votes do not know the boundary marks, which would result in the loss of robes and the violation of the summer retreat.
Generally, there are three ways of granting consent (*chanda*):
first, granting consent for purity when the precepts are recited;
second, granting consent for the invitation (*pravāraṇā*) during the ceremony of self-invitation.
Third, in all other *karmavācanā* procedures, it is simply stated that one "gives consent" (*chanda*).
Regarding the text for the *karmavācanā* for establishing a great boundary (*mahā-sīmā*): "Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
This bhikṣu so-and-so of this residence proclaims the marks of the four directions of the great boundary."

If the time is ripe for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha listen with patience: the Saṃgha now establishes a great boundary within these four markers, constituting a single residence and a single recitation of the Prātimokṣa.
The motion is as follows:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
This bhikṣu so-and-so of this residence announces the marks of the great boundary (mahā-sīmā) in the four directions."
The Saṃgha now establishes a great boundary (mahā-sīmā) within these four directional markers, constituting a single residential area and a single recitation of the precepts.

Those elders who consent to the Saṃgha’s establishment of a great boundary within these four directional markers as a single residential area and a single recitation of the precepts should remain silent; those who do not consent should speak.

"The Saṃgha has consented to establish a great boundary (mahā-sīmā) within these four marks, as a single residence and for a single recitation of the Prātimokṣa; the establishment of the great boundary is complete.
Because the Saṃgha consents by remaining silent, this matter shall be held thus."

The *karmavācanā* for the formal act of delimiting a *sīmā*: Originally, the establishment of a *sīmā* arose because it was difficult for a large assembly at a residence to gather; therefore, this boundary was separately delimited so that when there are essential matters among the assembly, they may be carried out at any time. Consequently, it cannot be dissolved immediately.

If one does not rely on a permanent dwelling place but performs the ritual only for a temporary period, the boundary is automatically dissolved once the task is completed; it is not permissible to fail to dissolve it, as doing so incurs an offense because it obstructs others from establishing their own boundaries.
"Venerable Sangha, listen!
This bhikṣu [Name], residing here, has proclaimed the marks of the small boundary for the four directions.

If the time is right for the Sangha and the Sangha permits, let the Sangha now establish a *karmavācanā* site (*sīmāmaṇḍala*) within these proclaimed marks of the small boundary for the four directions."
The motion is as follows:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
This bhikṣu so-and-so, residing at this location, has declared the marks of the small boundary on all four sides."
The Saṃgha now intends to establish a *karmavācanā* boundary (*sīmā*) within these marks of the small four-sided boundary here.
Those elders who consent to the Saṃgha’s establishment of this *śīlaskandha* boundary within these four-sided marks, let them remain silent; those who do not consent, let them speak.
"The Saṃgha has already consented to the establishment of the *sīmā-bandha* (boundary) within these four directional marks.
Because the Saṃgha consents by remaining silent, this matter is thus upheld.

Regarding the ritual text for dissolving the Great Boundary (*mahāsīma*) and the *śīma-bandha*: since this single ritual act (*karmavācanā*) serves to dissolve both boundaries, the text simply states "dissolving the boundary" (*sīma-uddharaṇa*). Thus, the name is not restricted to one or the other; the significance lies therein.

When performing the current ritual, the boundary for the *sīmā* (precept field) is dissolved according to the specific matter at hand; the only difference is that those who reside together must recite the *Poṣadha* together.
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!..."
"Venerable sirs, at this present dwelling place, the bhikṣus share the same residence and the same recitation of the precepts.
If the Saṃgha’s time has come and the Saṃgha is willing to grant its consent, let the boundary be dissolved.
Thus is the motion.
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
These bhikṣus residing at this same dwelling place and observing the same *poṣadha* recitation now dissolve the boundary (*sīmā*).

Whichever elders among you consent to the Saṃgha dissolving the boundary for those residing at this same dwelling place and observing the same *poṣadha* recitation, remain silent; whoever does not consent, speak."
"The Saṃgha has consented; having resolved the boundary for those dwelling in the same residence and reciting the Prātimokṣa together, it is concluded.
Since the Saṃgha consents by remaining silent, this matter is thus upheld."

The *karmavācanā* for establishing the boundary for not losing one's robe (*akṣayanivāsana-sīmā*) is as follows: Since this boundary for not losing one's robe is established based on the characteristics of the great boundary (*mahāsīmā*) and possesses no distinct characteristics of its own, the text still refers to it by the name of this residential site.
If there is a village, one must exclude the village; if there is no village, it is unnecessary to chant "excluding the village" or "outside the village boundary.
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
This dwelling place is a single dwelling place with a single recitation of the precepts."
"If it is the time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to listen, let the Saṃgha now establish the 'boundary of not losing one's robe,' excluding villages and the areas outside of villages.
The motion is made thus:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!..."
This dwelling place is a single dwelling place with a single recitation of the *Prātimokṣa*.
The Saṃgha now establishes a boundary for not losing one's robe (*akathina-sīmā*), excluding villages and the space outside of villages.

Those elders who consent to the Saṃgha’s establishment of this boundary for not losing one's robe at this dwelling place—a single dwelling place with a single recitation of the *Prātimokṣa*, excluding villages and the space outside of villages—should remain silent; those who do not consent should speak.
“The Saṃgha has consented to establish a boundary for not losing one’s robes within the same residence and the same recitation of the Prātimokṣa, excluding the village and its surrounding area.
Since the Saṃgha consents by remaining silent, this matter is thus upheld.”

The Ritual Text for Dissolving the *Akaṭhina-cīvara* Boundary: Since the Great Boundary (*mahā-sīmā*) and the *Akaṭhina-cīvara* Boundary are established as a single location through successive consecrations, the procedures for dissolving and binding them differ from one another.
If one wishes to dissolve [the boundaries], one should first dissolve the *acīvarāpattika-sīmā* (the boundary for not losing robes), and then dissolve the *mahāsīmā* (the great boundary).
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
In this residence, the bhikṣus share the same dwelling place and the same recitation of the Prātimokṣa."
"If it is the time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha permits, let the Saṃgha now dissolve the 'no-loss-of-clothing' boundary (*akalpiya-vastra-sīmā*).
Thus is the motion (*jñapti*).
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!..."

"Venerable sirs, for this community of bhikṣus dwelling together in one residence and performing the recitation of the Prātimokṣa together, the Sangha now dissolves the *akopyaka-sīmā* (the boundary for not losing one's robe).

Those elders who consent to the Sangha’s dissolution of the *akopyaka-sīmā* for those dwelling together in one residence and performing the recitation of the Prātimokṣa together, remain silent; whoever does not consent, please speak."
The Sangha has consented; the boundary for not losing one's robes, established within a single residence and a single recitation of the Prātimokṣa, is hereby dissolved.
Since the Sangha consents by remaining silent, this matter is thus upheld.

The *karmavācanā* for the formal act of delimiting a small boundary (*kṣudrasīmābandhana*): If, on the day of the *poṣadha*, various bhikṣus are traveling along a road through villages or wilderness and wish to recite the precepts, but because they are numerous it is difficult to assemble them, they are unable to achieve concord.

They should listen to and follow their teacher, virtuous friends, and spiritual mentors; they may descend from the path and assemble separately in one place to establish a minor boundary (*kṣudrasīmā*) and recite the *Prātimokṣa*.
There is no need to chant the boundaries (*sīmā-lakṣaṇa*), as the boundary is established by a small number of people.
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
There are currently this many bhikṣus assembled.
If it is the proper time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to grant its consent, let us establish a small boundary (sīmā)."
The motion is as follows:
"Venerable Sangha, listen!
Now so many bhikṣus have gathered to establish a small boundary."
"Venerable sirs, those who consent to the assembly of these many bhikṣus to establish a small boundary (sīmā) remain silent; those who do not consent speak.
The Saṃgha has already consented, and the assembly of these many bhikṣus to establish the small boundary is concluded.
"Since the Saṃgha consents and remains silent, this matter shall be held thus.
If there are four people, one says "four people"; if five people, one says "five people," and so on; because the number is not fixed, one says "so many bhikṣus have assembled."
The Karmavācanā for Dissolving a Small Boundary: "Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
There are now this many bhikṣus assembled.
If the time is right for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha permits, let us dissolve the small boundary at this location."
The motion is as follows:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
Now there are so many bhikṣus assembled to dissolve this small boundary at this location."
"Venerable sirs, those who consent to the Sangha's dissolution of this small boundary here remain silent; those who do not consent should speak.
The Sangha has consented and completed the dissolution of this small boundary here.
"Since the Saṃgha consents by remaining silent, this matter is thus upheld.

Regarding the method for establishing a small boundary (*kṣudrasīmā*) for the *pravāraṇā*: if one is not in a village, nor in a forest hermitage (*āraṇya*), nor traveling on a road, and wishes to perform the *pravāraṇā*, but those who are not of like mind cannot perform the *pravāraṇā* in assembly, they should establish a small boundary in a separate location together with their teachers, close friends, and associates to perform the *pravāraṇā*.
This space is already fully occupied by the monks sitting here; there is no need to announce the boundaries.
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
The seating places for the bhikṣus are already full, extending as far as these seating places of the bhikṣus."
"If it is the time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to listen, let the Saṃgha establish a small boundary at this location.
Thus is the formal motion (*jñapti*).
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
"Marking off the area where these bhikṣus are seated, the Saṃgha shall establish a small boundary (sīmā) here.
Those elders who consent to the Saṃgha establishing a small boundary within this area marked by the seating of these bhikṣus, remain silent; those who do not consent, speak."
"The Sangha has consented; the small boundary has been established for the seating area of these bhikṣus.
Since the Sangha consents by remaining silent, this matter is thus upheld."

The *karmavācanā* for the formal act (*karmavastu*) of establishing a common boundary for the recitation of the *Poṣadha* and the sharing of material offerings: If two residences are currently separate from one another, and they now wish to merge them so as to share a common *Poṣadha* recitation and a common distribution of offerings, they must first dissolve their respective original boundaries. Subsequently, the two residences shall jointly erect boundary markers to combine them into a single boundary.
The Saṃgha assembles in one place to perform the formal act (*karmavācanā*) for establishing the boundary:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
As has been described regarding the characteristics of the precepts..."
"If it is the time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to listen, let us, at this place and that place, establish a common recitation of the Prātimokṣa and a common distribution of offerings.
Thus is the motion.
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!

According to the characteristics of the boundary as they have been described, the Saṃgha now establishes at this place and that place a single recitation of the Prātimokṣa and a single distribution of offerings."

"Whichever elders among you consent to the Saṃgha binding a boundary at this place and that place for a single recitation of the Prātimokṣa and a single distribution of offerings, remain silent; whoever does not consent, speak."

"The Sangha has already consented to this boundary, where at these various places there is a single recitation of the *Poṣadha* and a single distribution of offerings; the formal demarcation of the boundary is completed.
Since the Sangha consents by remaining silent, this matter shall be maintained as such."

The ritual text for the *karmavācanā* of establishing a common boundary for the recitation of the *Poṣadha* while maintaining separate distributions of offerings (*lābha*) is as follows: First, both parties dissolve their respective original boundaries; subsequently, the two residences are joined by erecting boundary markers together to form a single boundary.
The entire Saṃgha assembles in one place and performs the formal act (*karmavācanā*) to demarcate it:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
Such are the boundary marks of the area as they have been described."
"If it is the time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to listen, let the Saṃgha now establish this place as one for the recitation of the Prātimokṣa, with separate offerings.
Thus is the motion.
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!"
Regarding the boundaries and characteristics as they have been described, the Saṃgha now establishes within this area a common recitation of the Prātimokṣa and separate distribution of offerings.

Those elders who consent to the Saṃgha establishing within these four boundaries a common recitation of the Prātimokṣa and separate distribution of offerings, remain silent; those who do not consent, speak.
"The Saṃgha has already consented to establish within these four boundaries a single recitation of the Prātimokṣa, while maintaining separate offerings.
Since the Saṃgha consents by remaining silent, this matter shall be held as such."

If two residences previously shared both the recitation of the precepts and the distribution of offerings, or shared the recitation of the precepts but had separate distributions of offerings, and they later wish to become separate again, they should first dissolve the boundary (*sīmā*). Thereafter, each shall individually proclaim the characteristics of their own boundary and re-establish them separately according to the old rules.
The Ritual Text for the Formal Act (*karmavācanā*) of Establishing Separate Recitation of the Precepts with a Unified Distribution of Offerings:

"Venerable Saṃgha, listen! If the time is right for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to grant its consent, let the Saṃgha now establish separate recitations of the precepts at these two respective residences, while maintaining a unified distribution of offerings, for the purpose of protecting the residences."
The motion is as follows:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
The Saṃgha now, at this and that residence, establishes a separate recitation of the Prātimokṣa while sharing the same material support, for the purpose of protecting the residence."

"Which elders consent that the Saṃgha, at this and that residence, shall establish a separate recitation of the Prātimokṣa while sharing the same distribution of offerings, for the sake of protecting the residence?"
"Those who approve of this remain silent; those who do not approve may speak.

The Sangha has approved of this: at that residence, the separate recitation of the Prātimokṣa is established, with a common distribution of offerings, for the purpose of protecting the residence. This is concluded.
"Since the Saṃgha consents by remaining silent, this matter is thus upheld. **2.
The Method for Receiving the Precepts** The second section: The Method for Ordaining a Śrāmaṇera. If one wishes to have their hair shaved within a saṃghārāma, they must inform the entire Saṃgha.
If the community is not in assembly, one should inform each individual dwelling and, once they have been informed, shave the hair.
If the community is in assembly, a formal motion (*jñapti*) must be made; only after the motion has been made may the hair be shaved.
One should announce as follows:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
This person, so-and-so, wishes to have his hair shaved by so-and-so."
"If the time is right for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha grant its consent to shave the hair of so-and-so.
Thus is the formal announcement (*jñapti*).
If one wishes to ordain someone by having them enter the monastery, one must announce this to the entire Saṃgha; once the announcement has been made, they may then be permitted to go forth.
One should announce it as follows:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
This person, so-and-so, seeks to go forth from home under the guidance of so-and-so."
"If the time has come for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha grant its consent to let so-and-so go forth.
Having made this formal announcement (*jñapti*) in this manner, he is ordained.
Instruct them to put on the *kāṣāya*, baring the right shoulder, remove their leather sandals, place the right knee on the ground, and join their palms, instructing them to speak as follows:
"I, [Name], take refuge in the Buddha, take refuge in the Dharma, and take refuge in the Saṃgha."
"Following the Buddha into homelessness, with [Name] as my preceptor, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, is my World-Honored One.
Thus he says three times.
“I, [Name], have completed taking refuge in the Buddha; I have completed taking refuge in the Dharma; I have completed taking refuge in the Saṃgha.
I have completed following the Buddha forth from home, with [Name] as my preceptor. The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, is my World-Honored One.”
Thus he says three times:
"For as long as life lasts, you must not kill living beings.
This is a śrāmaṇera precept; can you uphold it?"
He replied, "I can. [The Buddha said:
"For as long as life lasts, you must not steal."
"Can you uphold these śrāmaṇera precepts?
He replied, "I can."
"For as long as life lasts, one must not engage in sexual misconduct.
This is a śrāmaṇera precept; can you uphold it?
He replied:
"Yes. "For as long as life lasts, you must not speak falsely.
This is a śrāmaṇera precept; can you uphold it?"
He replied, "I can. [The Buddha said:
"For as long as life lasts, you must not drink alcohol."
"Can you uphold these śrāmaṇera precepts?
He replied, "I can."
"For as long as life lasts, you must not wear flower garlands or anoint your body with fragrant oils.
This is a śrāmaṇera precept; can you uphold it?
He replied:
“Yes. “For as long as life lasts, you must not engage in singing, dancing, or theatrical performances, nor go to witness them intentionally.
This is a śrāmaṇera precept; can you uphold it?”
He replied, "I can.
"For as long as life lasts, you must not sit upon high or wide beds."
"Can you uphold these śrāmaṇera precepts?
He replied, "I can."

3. The Method for the Removal of Offenses. This third section on the removal of offenses concerns the method for repenting of *saṃghāvaśeṣa* (saṃghādisesa) offenses. Since these offenses of the second category are grave, one must undergo repentance before the assembly and practice the methods of discipline (*vinaya*) to rectify the heart.
However, the methods for subduing [transgressions] necessarily consist of two types:
first, the remediation of faults; second, the remediation of offenses.
Regarding the initial *saṃvaraṇa-karman* (the rite of concealment), it is for the purpose of remedying a fault, not for the purpose of remedying an offense.
When performing the *parivāsa* (concealment) *karmavācanā*, one must first repent for the *duṣkṛta* offenses of concealment before the formal procedure of *parivāsa* is administered.
The six-night period and the subsequent *ābṛhaṇa* (expiation of the offense) are the two methods for treating the offense, as they constitute the actual repentance for the *saṃghāvaśeṣa*.
Regarding those who conceal their offense, they must undergo three types of *karmavācanā*;
regarding those who do not conceal it, they receive only the six-night penance (*ṣaḍrātra*) and the restoration from guilt (*āpattivyutthāna*).

"Venerable sirs, those who consent to the formal act (*karmavācanā*) for the rehabilitation from offense (*āpattivyutthāna*) of the bhikṣu so-and-so should remain silent; those who do not consent should speak.
This is the first formal act."
The second and third [proclamations] are also spoken in this manner.
"The Saṃgha has already consented; the formal act (*karmavācanā*) for the removal of guilt for the monk so-and-so is completed.
Because the Saṃgha consents by remaining silent, this matter shall be held as such."

Regarding the method for repentance for the *naiḥsargika-pāyattika* offenses: because this third section involves the commission of two categories of offenses, it is supplemented by the *pratisaṃharaṇīya-dharma* (the method of subjugation), which requires that the item be relinquished within the Saṃgha.

If there are no monks at the residence, one may relinquish [the precepts] before three, two, or even one person; however, one must not relinquish them before a separate group, as such an act does not constitute a valid relinquishment.
The Text for Relinquishing a *Naiḥsargika-pāyattika* Robe within the Saṃgha: "Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
I, the bhikṣu [Name], intentionally kept this surplus robe for more than ten days, thereby committing an offense of *naiḥsargika-pāyattika*. I now relinquish it to the Saṃgha."
"I now relinquish it to the Saṃgha.
A second and a third time, he should speak in this same manner.
Having relinquished it, he should immediately perform confession within the Saṃgha.
The Text for Requesting Confession from the Sangha: "Venerable Sangha, listen!
I, the bhikṣu [Name], intentionally kept this much extra robe for more than ten days, thereby committing an offense of *naiḥsargika-pāyattika*."
This robe has already been relinquished to the Saṃgha; I have committed such-and-such an offense and now request confession before the community of monks.
May the Saṃgha grant me, the bhikṣu [Name], permission for confession out of compassion.
A second and third time, he should speak in this same manner.
He should then invite one person from within the Saṃgha to perform the confession before him, go to the place of a pure bhikṣu, and make the following formal announcement (*jñapti*):
"I, the bhikṣu [Name], request the Venerable One to accept my confession."
The one receiving the confession should first inform the Saṃgha, and only then accept the confession.
The formal announcement made by the one receiving the confession within the Saṃgha is as follows: "Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
The bhikṣu [Name] intentionally kept such a number of extra robes for more than ten days, thereby committing an offense of forfeiture and transgression."
This robe has already been relinquished to the Saṃgha; I have committed such-and-such an offense and now repent before the community of monks.
If it is the proper time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha permits, may I accept the confession of the bhikṣu [Name].
The formal announcement is as follows.
The Text for Confession Before One Person in the Sangha: "Virtuous One, please attend to me with one-pointed mind!
I, the bhikṣu [Name], intentionally kept such an extra robe for more than ten days, thereby committing an offense of forfeiture and confession (naiḥsargika-pāyattika)."
This robe has already been relinquished to the Saṃgha. Now, having committed such-and-such an offense, I now repent before the Venerable Ones;

I dare not conceal it. Through repentance there is peace and happiness; without repentance there is no peace and happiness. Recalling my transgression, I disclose it; knowing it, I dare not conceal it.
"Venerable sir, remember me as pure, complete in the aggregate of precepts, and having observed the pure *poṣadha*.
A second and a third time, it should be spoken in this same manner.
Having spoken thus, the one who receives the confession should say:
“Reproach your own mind and give rise to a sense of weary detachment.
He should then reply: “So be it.”
The *karmavācanā* for the Saṃgha returning the robe to this bhikṣu, according to the procedure for returning a robe following a *niḥsargika-pāyattika* offense:
If there is one who has kept the robe dyed, it should be returned through a formal act (*karmavācanā*) only after having been kept overnight;

however, if there is a valid reason, it is also permitted to perform the *karmavācanā* on the same day, provided that the robe must be entrusted to another person by specifically naming them, and may not be returned directly.
If there are no items kept through attachment, they must all be returned on that very day.

Now, regarding this offense of *naiḥsargika-pāyattika* for keeping an item beyond the permitted period, the formal ritual (*karmavācanā*) for returning the robe after it has been kept overnight is as follows:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!..."
The bhikṣu so-and-so intentionally kept this surplus robe for more than ten days, thereby committing an offense of *naiḥsargika-pāyattika*.
This robe has already been relinquished to the Saṃgha.
If the time is right for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha grant its consent; the Saṃgha now bestows this robe upon so-and-so, who shall in turn return it to the bhikṣu so-and-so.
The motion is as follows:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
The bhikṣu [Name], having intentionally kept this surplus robe for more than ten days, has committed an offense of expiation involving forfeiture."
This robe has already been relinquished to the Saṃgha.
The Saṃgha now holds this robe to give to [Name], who shall in turn return it to the bhikṣu [Name].
Those elders who consent to the Saṃgha holding this robe to give to [Name], who shall return it to the bhikṣu [Name], remain silent; those who do not consent, speak.
"The Sangha has consented; the Sangha has bestowed this robe upon so-and-so, and so-and-so shall return it to the bhikṣu so-and-so.
Since the Sangha consents by remaining silent, this matter is thus upheld.

The Text on the Formal Act of Renunciation Before Three, Two, or One Person: If the renunciation is performed before three, two, or one person, the procedure for renunciation is the same as above; the only difference is that one does not address the *saṃgha*.

Regarding the methods of confession for three people, two people, or one person: when receiving the confession from others, the recipient should speak to those standing nearby before accepting the confession.
When confessing to a single person, one simply relinquishes the transgression and performs the repentance directly.
Of the three persons, the one receiving the confession speaks to the person standing nearby: "Venerable sir, please listen as I receive the confession of the bhikṣu [Name].
The other replies: "So be it."
The method of confession is as described above.

Regarding the phrase "the method for confessing remaining offenses," "remaining offenses" refers to all other offenses besides those of the two preceding categories and the *naiḥsargika* [pāyattika], namely: the *pāyattika*, the two lower categories of offenses, the *sthūlātyaya*, the *duṣkṛta*, and so forth.
Among these remaining offenses, the *pāyattika* and *prātideśanīya* are all to be confessed face-to-face;
the offenses of the fifth category are all to be confessed mentally;
among the *sthūlātyaya* offenses, those that are grave are to be confessed before the assembly, while those that are minor are to be confessed face-to-face.
Therefore, the procedures for performing repentance differ according to the degree of the offense.

Regarding the text for confessing before a single bhikṣu: one should go to a pure bhikṣu, bare the right shoulder, and if he is a senior elder (sthavira), prostrate at his feet. Then, placing the right knee on the ground and joining the palms, one shall state the name of the offense and the category of the offense, speaking as follows:
"Venerable sir, please attend to me with a single mind!"
I, bhikṣu [name], have committed such-and-such an offense. I now confess it before the Elder; I dare not conceal it.
Through confession there is peace and happiness, while through non-confession there is no peace and happiness. I recall the offense and disclose it; knowing it, I do not conceal it.
"Venerable sir, remember me as being pure, complete in the aggregate of precepts, and having observed the Uposatha purely.
This should be said a second and a third time.
The one who accepts the confession should say:
"Reproach your own mind and give rise to weary detachment.
He replied, "So be it."
The procedure for the confession of two bhikṣus: They should go before two pure bhikṣus and request one bhikṣu to perform the confession on their behalf.
The one receiving the confession should first ask the second bhikṣu, saying:
"Venerable sir, please listen as this bhikṣu [name] confesses."
He replied, "So be it.
The method for his confession is the same as above.

The Procedure for Confession Before Three Bhikṣus: One should go to three bhikṣus who are pure and also request one bhikṣu to serve as the witness for the confession; the remaining details are the same as the method for the two persons mentioned above.

The Text for Confession Before the Saṃgha: One should go before the Saṃgha, bare the right shoulder, remove one’s leather sandals, and after prostrating at the feet of the monks, place the right knee on the ground and join the palms, making this declaration:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!..."
"I, Bhikṣu [Name], having committed such-and-such an offense, now request the Saṃgha for confession.
Thus he speaks three times.
Within the Saṃgha, he separately requests one person to perform the confession in his presence; he then goes to a pure Bhikṣu and speaks as follows:
"I, Bhikṣu [Name], request the Venerable One to accept my confession.
The one receiving the confession should first inform the Saṃgha, and only then accept the confession.
He should make the formal announcement (*jñapti*) as follows:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
That bhikṣu, so-and-so, has committed such-and-such an offense and now confesses it to the Saṃgha.
If the time is right for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha permits me, I shall accept the confession of the bhikṣu, so-and-so."
The announcement is made in this manner. Having made this announcement, the confession is received; the method for the repentance is the same as above.

Regarding the text for communal confession when the entire Saṃgha has committed the same offense: When it is time to recite the *Prātimokṣa* at the monastery and the entire Saṃgha has committed the same offense, those who have committed the offense may not confess to one another. Furthermore, as the time for the recitation approaches, it is not permitted to seek out pure monks from outside. Because the matter of the *Prātimokṣa* recitation is of great importance, the assembly is permitted to confess by means of a single formal motion (*jñapti*), after which the recitation of the precepts may proceed.
One should make the formal announcement (*jñapti*) as follows:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
This entire community of monks has committed an offense."
"If it is the time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to listen, let this entire Saṃgha perform confession.
Having made this formal announcement (*jñapti*) in this manner, one should then recite the precepts.

The Text for Confessing Doubtful Offenses: Having approached a pure bhikṣu, baring the right shoulder and removing the leather sandals, and having prostrated at the feet of the Saṃgha, he places his right knee on the ground, joins his palms, and announces the name of the precept he has violated, speaking these words:
"Venerable Sir, please take note!..."
"I have developed a doubt regarding a certain offense; I now declare it before the Venerable One.
When I am later free from doubt, I shall perform the confession according to the Dharma.

This text for the disclosure of a doubtful offense within the Saṃgha when the entire Saṃgha has committed the same offense should also be recited at the time of the *Poṣadha*. The disclosure of a doubtful offense is identical to the method of confession described above.
One should make the formal announcement (*jñapti*) as follows:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
This entire Saṃgha has doubts regarding its offenses."
"If it is the proper time for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha listen with patience: these members of the Saṃgha shall themselves confess their offenses.
Having made this formal announcement (*jñapti*) in this manner, one may then recite the precepts.

4. The Method for Proclaiming the Precepts (Śīla-uddeśa-dharma). This fourth section contains the texts for granting consent (*chanda*) and for purity (*pāriśuddhi*). Regarding matters concerning the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṃgha, as well as illness or tending to the sick, there is the method for granting consent and declaring purity.
"Venerable sir, please attend to me with one-pointed mind!
Today the community of monks performs the *poṣadha* and recites the precepts; I, [name], for the sake of a certain matter, grant my consent and purity regarding this legal business of the Saṃgha."
There are five ways of giving consent (*chanda*).
If one says:
"I give my consent to you."
If one says: "I speak of desire," or if one says:
"Tell me about desire," [he said].
[The other] either manifested its physical form or explained it in detail.
If [the formal act] is completed, the granting of consent (*chanda*) is valid; otherwise, it is not valid.
This is the same when granting consent during the *pravāraṇā* ceremony; the only difference is that one says, "I grant my consent for the *pravāraṇā*."
Regarding the text for the purification through the enjoyment of sensual desires: one may receive it according to the number of individuals whose names and clans one can remember.
Upon arriving among the Saṃgha, one should speak as follows:
"Venerable sirs, please attend to me with one-pointed mind!

"Many bhikṣus, for a certain reason, have granted me their consent and purification; I, along with those many bhikṣus, grant my consent and purification for the formal act of the Saṃgha performed in accordance with the Dharma."

Having received that *chanda* and *pārisuddhi* through the procedure of further transmission, because a matter has subsequently arisen for oneself, one transmits both that person’s and one’s own *chanda* and *pārisuddhi* to another person, saying:
"Venerable sir, attend with a single mind!..."

I, the bhikṣu [Name], together with many bhikṣus, have received the consent and purity (chanda-pārisuddhi). Now, having a matter of business, they and I myself grant our consent and purity for the legal matters of the Saṃgha.
The Text for the Poṣadha Precept Recitation: On the day of the Poṣadha, whether before the light meal or after the main meal, the Elder (upādhyāya) should announce:
"Today is the Poṣadha day; at this time, the Saṃgha being in harmony, let us assemble in such-and-such hall to recite the precepts."
If there are four or more persons, they should first make a formal announcement (*jñapti*), and only then recite the precepts.
The announcement is as described in the section on the precepts.
If there are three or two persons, they should face one another and together perform the *poṣadha* by means of three utterances, saying:
“Venerable sir, please attend to me with a single mind!
Today, on the fifteenth day, the Saṃgha recites the Prātimokṣa; I, [name], am pure.
Thus he says three times.
If there is only one person, he should mentally reflect and speak aloud:
"Today the Saṃgha recites the precepts on the fifteenth day; I, so-and-so, am pure.
This should be said three times.
The Text for Proclaiming Purity: There are three days for the *poṣadha*:
either the sixteenth, the fifteenth, or the fourteenth day.

Whether there are visiting or resident monks, whether they have already proclaimed their purity or not, whether they arrive earlier or later, and whether the assembly is large, small, or equal in number—[the procedure remains the same].
If the visiting monks have already recited the precepts and later resident monks arrive in equal numbers, the precepts must be recited again for all of them.
If the resident monks are fewer in number, they should go outside the boundary to recite the precepts.
If resident bhikṣus have already recited the precepts and subsequently many visiting bhikṣus arrive such that they outnumber the residents, the precepts should be recited again.
If the visiting bhikṣus are equal in number to the residents, they should themselves go outside the boundary to recite the precepts.
If the day for reciting the precepts is the same but the time differs, equality is determined by the number of new and resident monks and their order of arrival.
If resident monks have already recited the precepts and visiting monks arrive afterward, if the number of visitors is equal to or greater than the residents, they must all recite the precepts again.
If the visiting bhikṣus are few, they should announce their purity (*pārisuddhi*).

If the resident bhikṣus arrive after the visiting bhikṣus have recited the *Poṣadha*, and the newcomers are equal in number to those already present, the visiting bhikṣus must also recite the *Poṣadha* once more; if they are fewer, they should announce their purity and sit in order to listen.
Whether the entire assembly has not yet risen, or whether most have risen, whether the announcement is made or not, the meaning is the same as above.
The ritual for declaring purity (*pārisuddhi*) should be stated as follows:
"Venerable Sangha, listen!..."
"I, [Name], am pure.
Having spoken thus three times, they sit in order and listen.
Regarding the abbreviated text for the recitation of the precepts due to the arising of the eight difficulties and other circumstances: as for the "eight difficulties":

The danger of kings, the danger of thieves, the danger of fire, the danger of water, the danger of illness, the danger of humans, the danger of non-humans, and the danger of malevolent insects—these are the eight difficulties.

As for other circumstances: when the great assembly has gathered but there are few seats; or when many members of the assembly are ill; or when the assembly has gathered but the coverings over the seats are insufficient; or when it rains; or when the *poṣadha* is frequent; or when a matter of dispute arises; or when the discussion of Abhidharma, Vinaya, or the preaching of the Dharma has lasted for a long time at night.
If the dawn has not yet appeared, one should perform the *karmavācanā* and recite the *Poṣadha*;

if the dawn has already appeared, one may not accept a formal declaration of purity (*śuddhipratijñā*) from one who has stayed overnight for the purpose of performing the *karmavācanā* and reciting the *Poṣadha*.
Depending on the distance of the location, if it is possible to recite the precepts in detail, one should do so; otherwise, one shall be dealt with according to the Dharma.
If it may be spoken briefly, then speak briefly; otherwise, one shall be dealt with according to the Dharma.
If the matter is urgent and it is not possible to speak briefly, one should immediately rise from one's seat and depart.
Regarding the abbreviated recitation of the precepts:
after the introduction to the recitation has been spoken, the rest should be declared as:
"The Sangha has already heard [the precepts]."
If, after the introduction to the recitation of the precepts and the four *pārājika* rules have been spoken, the remainder should say:
"The Saṃgha has constantly heard [these].
In this manner, it continues until the *prātideśanīya* rules; for the remainder, they should likewise say: [“The Saṃgha has constantly heard [these]”].
“The Sangha has heard.
When the Sangha recites the precepts for the instruction of bhikṣuṇīs, the one reciting the precepts should ask:
“Who has sent the bhikṣuṇī to come and receive the instruction?”
The nun acting as the instructor shall announce to the Saṃgha, saying:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
The bhikṣuṇī-saṃgha, headed by [Name], being in harmony, prostrates at the feet of the venerable Saṃgha and requests instruction."
Thus it was said three times.
If there is anyone among the assembly qualified to provide instruction, they should be appointed;
if there is none, the Elder should personally provide the instruction and deliver the formal charge.
The Karmavācanā for Appointing a Bhikṣu to Instruct the Bhikṣuṇīs: "Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
If the time is right for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha permits, let the Saṃgha appoint the bhikṣu [Name] to instruct the bhikṣuṇīs."
The motion is as follows:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
The Saṃgha appoints the bhikṣu [Name] to instruct the bhikṣuṇīs."
"Whichever elders consent to the Saṃgha’s appointment of the bhikṣu so-and-so to instruct the bhikṣuṇīs, let them remain silent; whoever does not consent, let them speak.
The Saṃgha has already consented to the appointment of the bhikṣu so-and-so to instruct the bhikṣuṇīs.
"Since the Saṃgha has consented by remaining silent, this matter is thus upheld.
The person appointed should then go to the nunnery and instruct the bhikṣuṇīs to assemble.
First, I shall explain the eight things that do not violate the Dharma. What are these eight?
First, even a bhikṣuṇī who is a hundred years old, upon seeing a newly ordained bhikṣu, should rise to greet him, prostrate before him, and offer him a seat.
This Dharma should be respected and praised; for as long as life lasts, one must not violate it.
Second, a bhikṣuṇī should not revile or scold a bhikṣu, nor should she slander him by saying:
"He has broken the precepts, he has broken his views, or he has broken his dignified conduct."
This rule should be respected and praised; for as long as life lasts, it must not be transgressed.

Third: A bhikṣuṇī should not perform an act of formal accusation (*ukkhepana*), a reminder (*sāraṇīya*), or a formal admission (*pāṭidesanīya*) against a bhikṣu; she should not obstruct another’s search for an offense, nor the recitation of the *Prātimokṣa*, nor the *Pravāraṇā* ceremony;
she should not reprimand a bhikṣu, but rather a bhikṣu should reprimand a bhikṣuṇī.
This rule should be honored and praised; for as long as life lasts, one must not violate it.
Fourth, once a śikṣamāṇā has completed her training in the precepts, she shall request the full ordination from the community of bhikṣus.
This rule should be respected and praised; for as long as life lasts, it must not be transgressed.
Fifth, when a bhikṣuṇī commits a saṃghāvaśeṣa offense, she must undergo the mānatva penance before the two assemblies of the Saṃgha for half a month.
This rule should be respected and praised; for as long as life lasts, it must not be transgressed.
Sixth, a bhikṣuṇī must, every half-month, request instruction from the saṃgha.
This rule should be respected and praised; for as long as life lasts, it must not be transgressed.
Seventh: A bhikṣuṇī should not observe the summer retreat (varṣā) in a place where there is no community of bhikṣus.
This rule should be respected and praised; for as long as life lasts, it must not be transgressed.
Eighth: when the Bhikṣuṇī Saṃgha has completed its rainy-season retreat, they should request the three matters of self-examination (pravāraṇā) from within the Bhikṣu Saṃgha:
what was seen, what was heard, and what was suspected.
"This Dharma should be respected and praised; for as long as life lasts, one must not violate it.
Having thus explained the eight things that must not be violated, he may thereafter preach the Dharma according to his inclination.
This is the extensive teaching on the Dharma.
The Elder’s instructional decree stated in reply:
"There is no instructor here; the community of nuns should perform the *poṣadha* according to the Dharma, being diligent and not negligent."
When the nun arrives the following day, the one who received the entrustment should respond with a dispatch according to this same text.

This is the abbreviated teaching on the method for the rainy season retreat (*varṣā*). The Fifth Method for the Rainy Season Retreat: The *Karmavācanā* for the Appointment by the Saṃgha to Distribute Rooms and Bedding. "Listen, venerable Saṃgha!..."
"If it is the time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to grant its consent, let the Saṃgha appoint the bhikṣu [Name] to distribute the rooms and bedding.
Thus is the motion.
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
The Saṃgha appoints the bhikṣu [Name] to distribute the rooms and bedding.
Those elders who consent to the Saṃgha’s appointment of the bhikṣu [Name] to distribute the rooms and bedding should remain silent; those who do not consent should speak.
The Sangha has already consented to appoint the monk so-and-so to distribute the rooms and bedding.
Because the Sangha consents by remaining silent, this matter is thus upheld.

Regarding the method for assigning rooms: first, the administrative officer shall select one room; once it has been taken, he shall inform the Elder (Sthavira) regarding the remaining rooms, requesting him to take them in order, saying:
"Venerable Elder!..."
"Such excellent rooms and bedding may be taken according to one's own preference.
First, the room is given to the senior monk (*sthavira*); next, it is given to the second, third, fourth, and so on, down to the junior monk (*navaka*), in the same manner.
If the room is large, one should accommodate the visiting bhikṣu.
The text for the *varṣā* (rainy season retreat) is as follows: "Venerable sir, attend to me with a single mind!
I, the bhikṣu [Name], shall observe the three-month summer *varṣā* residence in dependence upon this village, this monastery, and this dwelling."
"The dwellings are dilapidated; they must be repaired.
A second and third time, he spoke thus:
"Relying upon [the name] who upholds the Vinaya, if there is any matter of doubt, you should go to him and ask."
The procedure for the later retreat (*paścimikā varṣā*) is also according to this same rule, with the sole difference that one says "later retreat.
The text for receiving the seven-day leave is as follows: "Venerable sir, please attend to me with a single mind!

I, the bhikṣu [name], having received the seven-day leave, am going outside the boundary for the sake of a certain matter, and shall return here to observe the retreat. I inform the Venerable sir so that he may know."
The second and third times were also spoken in this manner.
The ritual procedure for the formal act (*karmavācanā*) of accepting [the robe] after seven days is found in the *Vinaya-mūla*, in the *Campā-khandhaka*.
Judging by this, it is evident that the old version of the *Karmavācanā* text is insufficient; therefore, it should be carefully compared and corrected to accord with the authentic standard.
The *Karmavācanā* for requesting the [extension of] the seven-day period is as follows: "Venerable Saṃgha, listen!..."

I, Bhikṣu [Name], having entered the summer retreat at this location, now request from the Saṃgha the formal act (*karmavācanā*) for receiving the *saptarātra-anujñā*—the permission to remain outside the boundary for seven days, fifteen days, or one month—for the sake of a certain matter, so that I may return to this very place to continue the retreat. I now beg the Saṃgha to grant me the formal act for receiving the *saptarātra-anujñā* for fifteen days or one month.
"I pray that the Saṃgha will grant me, the bhikṣu [Name], the formal act (*karmavācanā*) for the seven-day period, or the fifteen-day or one-month period, out of compassion.
The second and third [requests] are also spoken in this manner.
The Ritual Text for Granting the *Saptāha-atikrānta* (Seven-Day) Procedure: "Venerable Saṃgha, listen!

The bhikṣu [Name], having entered the summer retreat at this location, has received the *saptāha-atikrānta* procedure for fifteen days or one month to go outside the boundary for a certain matter, with the intention of returning here to continue the retreat. He now requests from the Saṃgha the formal act (*karmavācanā*) to receive the *saptāha-atikrānta* procedure for fifteen days or one month."

If the time has come for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to listen, let the Saṃgha now grant the bhikṣu [Name] the formal act (*karmavācanā*) of receiving the "seven-day-at-most" rule, whether for fifteen days or one month.
The motion is as follows:
"Venerable Sangha, listen!

If a bhikṣuṇī, with a defiled mind, engages in physical contact with a man who has a defiled mind—anywhere from below the armpits to above the knees—whether by rubbing, pressing, stroking upward, stroking downward, pulling, pushing, lifting up, lowering down, grasping, or pressing firmly;
she is no longer a bhikṣuṇī, nor is she a daughter of the Śākya clan."
"Within this, for as long as life lasts, you must not commit any violation;
can you uphold this? He replied, "I can."
"One must not commit the eight offenses, even down to [acting] with an animal. If a bhikṣuṇī, with a defiled mind,

consents to a man with a defiled mind to take her hand, take her garment, go to a secluded place, stand in a secluded place, speak in a secluded place, walk together, have their bodies touch, or make a mutual appointment—
if she commits any of these eight things, she is no longer a bhikṣuṇī, nor a daughter of the Śākya clan."
"Within this, for as long as life lasts, you must not commit any transgression.
Can you uphold this? He replied, "I can."
"One should not conceal the offenses of others, even down to a *duṣkṛta* or a verbal transgression.
If a bhikṣuṇī knows that another bhikṣuṇī has committed a *pārājika* offense, she must not fail to report it herself, nor inform the Saṃgha, nor tell anyone else so that they may know."
Later, at another time, if this bhikṣuṇī has abandoned the path, or has been expelled, or has become one who does not live in communion, or has entered among the followers of external paths;
she later speaks thus:
"I already knew that this person was such and such."
"She is not a bhikṣuṇī, nor is she a daughter of the Śākya clan, for she conceals a grave offense.
For as long as life lasts, you must not commit this; can you uphold it?"
He replied, "I can. [The Buddha said:
"You must not follow the words of the monk who has been suspended, nor even those of a śrāmaṇera."

If a bhikṣuṇī knows that a bhikṣu has been formally accused by the Saṃgha in accordance with the Dharma, in accordance with the Vinaya, and in accordance with the Buddha’s instructions, for an offense against proper conduct, and that he has not yet performed repentance nor been granted the status of living together;
yet she nevertheless associates with and follows that bhikṣu.
That bhikṣuṇī should admonish this bhikṣuṇī, saying: "Sister! That bhikṣu has been formally accused by the Saṃgha;

he has acted contrary to the Dharma, contrary to the Vinaya, and contrary to what the Buddha has taught, having violated the rules of decorum and not yet made amends, and thus he does not dwell in communion."
"Do not follow that bhikṣuṇī.
When that bhikṣuṇī admonishes this bhikṣuṇī and she persists in her refusal to relinquish [her position],
that bhikṣuṇī should admonish her up to three times so that she may abandon this matter.
Up to three admonitions, if she relinquishes [the offense], it is well;
if she does not relinquish it, she is no longer a bhikṣuṇī, nor a daughter of the Śākya clan, having committed the offense of "following the formal accusation.
Within this, for as long as life lasts, you must not commit this; can you uphold it?
He replied, “I can.
“Listen attentively, noble woman!
The Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha has taught the four reliances; it is the rule for bhikṣuṇīs that they rely upon these when going forth and receiving full ordination.
"To go forth and receive full ordination by relying on rag-robes is the Dharma of a bhikṣuṇī.
Can you maintain this for as long as life lasts?
She replied:
"Yes. "If one obtains extra benefits—
whether it be robes offered by a donor, light robes, or robes made of cut pieces— one should accept them."
"Living by alms-seeking, having gone forth, and receiving full ordination—this is the Dharma of a bhikṣuṇī.
Can you maintain this for as long as life lasts?
She replies:
“Yes. “If one receives long-term benefits—

such as food assigned by the Saṃgha, food sent by a donor, food on the eighth day of the month, food on the fifteenth day, food on the first day of the month, the regular food of the community of monks, or food offered at a donor’s invitation— one may accept it.”
"Sitting under a tree for one's dwelling and receiving the full ordination as a renunciant—this is the Dharma of a bhikṣuṇī.
Can you uphold this for as long as life lasts?
She replied:
“Yes. “If one obtains long-term benefits— such as a separate room,
a multi-storied pavilion, a small room, a stone cave, or two rooms with a single door— one should accept them.”
"It is the rule for bhikṣuṇīs to go forth and receive full ordination using medicinal herbs that have undergone decomposition.
Can you maintain this throughout your entire life?
She replied:
“Yes. “If one obtains long-term benefits—
namely, ghee, oil, fresh butter, honey, or rock honey— one should accept them.”

“You have now completed receiving the precepts; the formal procedure of the *jñapti-caturtha-karman* has been accomplished according to the Dharma; you have obtained your place; the Upādhyāya is according to the Dharma; the Ācārya is according to the Dharma; and the two assemblies of the Saṃgha are fully complete.”

You should properly receive the teachings; you should diligently make offerings to the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Sangha; and regarding all lawful instructions from your preceptors and teachers, you must not, under any circumstances, act in opposition to them.

One should study, recite the sutras, and diligently seek skillful means so as to attain the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship within the Buddha-dharma.
Since you have only just left the household life, your efforts will not be in vain, and the fruits of your retribution will never cease.
As for other matters you do not yet know, you should ask your Upādhyāya and Ācārya.

Section Three: The Method for Expiating Offenses. Regarding the method for nuns to confess *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offenses: because nuns are female and weak, they must rely on external support; therefore, the number of days [of probation] is increased.
If one harbors evil for the sake of private interests, one ruins oneself and ruins others, as the offense is not to be taken lightly.

When a *bhikṣuṇī* conceals a *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offense, she merely incurs an increased penalty of discipline: she must practice *mānatva* for half a month, as there is no separate method of disciplinary subjugation for concealment.

Regarding the confession of a *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offense by a bhikṣuṇī, it must be performed through the *mānatva* *karma* within the assembly of both orders; the two orders—the monks and the nuns—must each consist of at least four members.
If the *karma* for absolving her of the offense is to be performed, there must be at least twenty members in each of the two orders—the monks and the nuns—and they may not be fewer than that.

The Text for the Formal Act (*karmavācanā*) of Requesting *Mānatva*: When a bhikṣuṇī has committed a saṃghāvaśeṣa offense, she must undergo *mānatva* for half a month within the two assemblies of the Saṃgha.

While undergoing *mānatva*, she should go before the two assemblies, bare her right shoulder, remove her leather sandals, prostrate at the feet of the Saṃgha, place her right knee on the ground, join her palms, and make this request as follows:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
I, the bhikṣuṇī [Name], have committed [Number] saṃghāvaśeṣa offenses. I now request from the dual Saṃghas the half-month *mānatva*."
"I pray that the Sangha will grant me a half-month *mānatva*, out of compassion.
Thus he says three times.
The ritual text for granting the *mānatva*: "Venerable Sangha, listen!
This bhikṣuṇī [Name], having committed [Number] saṃghāvaśeṣa offenses, now requests from the Saṃgha of both divisions the *mānatva* penance for half a month.
If it is the proper time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to grant its consent, let the Saṃgha now bestow upon the bhikṣuṇī [Name] the *mānatva* penance for half a month.
The motion is as follows:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
This bhikṣuṇī [Name], having committed [Number] saṃghāvaśeṣa offenses, now requests from the dual Saṃghas a half-month of *mānatva*."
The Sangha now grants a half-month *mānatva* penance to the bhikṣuṇī [Name].
Those elders who consent to the Sangha granting a half-month *mānatva* penance to the bhikṣuṇī [Name] should remain silent; those who do not consent should speak.
This is the first *karmavācanā*.
Thus it is said three times.
The Saṃgha has already granted the *mānatva* for half a month to the bhikṣuṇī [Name]; this is concluded.
"Since the Saṃgha consents by remaining silent, this matter is thus upheld.

The procedure for a bhikṣuṇī practicing *mānatva* is the same as that for the monks above; however, she must perform the formal announcement (*jñapti*) in this manner every day before both divisions of the Saṃgha.
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
I, the bhikṣuṇī [Name], have committed [Number] saṃghāvaśeṣa offenses. I have already requested from the Saṃgha of both divisions the half-month *mānatva* penance;
the Saṃgha has already granted me the half-month *mānatva*."
I, Bhikṣuṇī [Name], having already practiced for several days, with several days remaining, inform the venerable Saṃgha so that they may know: I am practicing mānatva.
The Text for Requesting the *karmavācanā* for Expiation: When a bhikṣuṇī has completed the half-month *mānatva*, she should go before the dual assembly (*ubhayasaṃgha*) and make this request:
"Venerable Saṃgha, please listen!"
I, the bhikṣuṇī [Name], have committed [Number] saṃghāvaśeṣa offenses of such-and-such a kind; I have already requested from the Saṃgha of both divisions the half-month mānatva penance;
the Saṃgha has already granted me the half-month mānatva.
I have already completed the half-month *mānatva* penance before the dual Saṃgha; I now request from the Saṃgha the formal act (*karmavācanā*) for the removal of my offense.
May the Saṃgha grant me the formal act for the removal of my offense, out of compassion.
Thus it was said three times.
The text for the *karmavācanā* for the absolution of offenses (*āpattivyutthāna*) is as follows:

"Venerable Saṃgha, listen! This bhikṣuṇī, so-and-so, has committed such-and-such a number of *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offenses and has already requested from the Saṃghas of both divisions a half-month of *mānatva*."
The Saṃgha has already granted the bhikṣuṇī [Name] a half-month *mānatva*.
This bhikṣuṇī [Name], having completed the half-month *mānatva* within both divisions of the Saṃgha, now requests from the Saṃgha the formal act (*karmavācanā*) for the removal of her offense.
"If it is the time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to listen, let the Saṃgha now perform the *karmavācanā* for the removal of the offense for the bhikṣuṇī so-and-so.
Thus is the motion.
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!"
This bhikṣuṇī [Name], having committed [Number] saṃghāvaśeṣa offenses, has already requested from the Saṃgha of both divisions a half-month *mānatva*;
the Saṃgha has already granted this bhikṣuṇī [Name] a half-month *mānatva*.
This bhikṣuṇī [Name], having already completed the half-month *mānatva* penance before the two assemblies of the Saṃgha, now requests from the Saṃgha the *karmavācanā* for the removal of her offense;
the Saṃgha now grants the *karmavācanā* for the removal of the offense to this bhikṣuṇī [Name].
"Venerable sirs, those who consent to this *karmavācanā* for the removal of the offense of the nun so-and-so by the Saṃgha, remain silent; those who do not consent, speak.
This is the first *karmavācanā*.
The second and third [motions] are also stated in this manner.
"The Saṃgha has already consented; the formal act (*karmavācanā*) for the removal of offense for the bhikṣuṇī so-and-so is completed.
Because the Saṃgha consents by remaining silent, this matter is thus upheld."

4. The Procedure for the Recitation of the Precepts (Poṣadha-karma). Fourth: Regarding this procedure for the recitation of the precepts, the first point is identical to that of the Great Saṃgha [of monks] above.

As for the *karmavācanā* for the Bhikṣuṇī Saṃgha to appoint a person to request instruction (*śikṣamāṇā-vinaya-śikṣā-prārthaka*): since the Bhikṣuṇī Saṃgha must go before the Great Saṃgha every half-month to request instruction and admonition, it is now necessary to appoint this messenger to request instruction on behalf of the Bhikṣuṇīs. The appointment should be made as follows.
“Sisters of the Sangha, listen!

If the time has come for the Sangha and the Sangha is willing to grant its consent, let the Sangha now appoint the bhikṣuṇī [Name] to go, on behalf of the bhikṣuṇī Saṃgha, once every half-month to the community of bhikṣus to request instruction.”
The motion is as follows:
"Venerable Sisters of the Saṃgha, listen!
The Saṃgha now appoints the bhikṣuṇī [Name] to go, for the sake of the bhikṣuṇī Saṃgha, once every half-month to the assembly of bhikṣus to request instruction."

Whichever sisters among you approve of the Saṃgha appointing the nun so-and-so to go to the community of monks every half-month on behalf of the community of nuns to seek instruction, remain silent; whoever does not approve, speak.
The Saṃgha has already consented to appoint the bhikṣuṇī so-and-so to go, for the sake of the bhikṣuṇī-saṃgha, once every half-month to the assembly of bhikṣus to seek instruction; this is concluded.
“Since the Saṃgha has consented by remaining silent, this matter is thus upheld.

Then, another person shall be appointed as a companion to go among the great assembly of monks to where the resident bhikṣu is staying; there, prostrating at his feet, bowing the body with the head lowered, and joining the palms, he shall speak these words:
“Venerable One, please attend to me with one-pointed mind!”
"The community of bhikṣuṇīs, such-and-such [number], being in harmony, prostrates at the feet of the community of bhikṣus and requests instruction.
The second and third times, it is spoken in the same manner.
When the bhikṣu who has received the entrustment recites the precepts, he should make the following formal announcement:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
The community of bhikṣuṇīs, such-and-such a group, being in harmony, prostrates at the feet of the venerable Saṃgha and requests instruction."
Thus it was said three times.
On the following day, the bhikṣuṇīs should inquire whether it is convenient;
the bhikṣu instructor should agree to go, and the bhikṣuṇīs should agree to meet the bhikṣu.
If one does not go when expected to do so, it is a *duṣkṛta*;
if the community of bhikṣuṇīs does not go out to welcome [the instructor] when expected to do so, it is a *duṣkṛta*.
If a bhikṣuṇī hears that the instructor is coming, she should go out to welcome him for half a *yojana* and escort him into the monastery, providing whatever he requires.
One should provide offerings of bathing requisites, soup and congee, food and drink, and fruits;
if one does not do so, it is a *duṣkṛta* offense.

If the entire community of bhikṣus is ill, or if the assembly is not in harmony, or if the number of members is incomplete, one should send a messenger to pay respects and inquire after their well-being.
If the community of bhikṣuṇīs is entirely ill, not in harmony, or if the assembly is incomplete, one must still send a messenger to pay respects and inquire after their welfare;
if one does not go, it is a duṣkṛta offense.

regarding the ritual text for appointing a member of the Bhikṣuṇī Saṃgha to go among the senior monks to receive the invitation. "Seen, heard, or suspected.
Thus it is reported.

what has been seen, heard, or suspected.

"The Saṃgha has already consented to appoint the bhikṣuṇī [Name] to go before the mahāsaṃgha on behalf of the bhikṣuṇī-saṃgha and announce the three matters of self-examination (pravāraṇā).
